Fixed Protocol Fixtures ​

These files provide stable inputs and expected results for the content draft. They were created on 2026-11-07 from the existing sample documents. The .pai files were generated with Python's standard library and are now used by the file, editor, and service checks.

FixtureContents and purpose
service, event, guideContent-model 0.6 data extracted from the three sample HTML files
layoutThree columns, explicit blank paragraphs, code, a table, two occurrences of one image, a background-image description, and an unreferenced asset
event-updatedThe same event document ID, revision 3, with the date changed from November 21 to November 28
event-conflict, event-staleDifferent content at an existing revision, and a previously unpublished older revision

Each set contains *.document.json (the HTML content object), *.package.json (the ZIP document.json object), and *.pai (the actual ZIP file). The original image bytes are retained. ZIP entries use Deflate and a fixed 1980-01-01 timestamp. Paths follow FORMAT.md.

hashes.json records the canonical JSON and expected SHA-256 digest for each document under the new algorithm. Checks normalize both asset representations and compare them with these values. Python independently checks SHA-256 of the recorded canonical JSON bytes. That check does not independently implement the complete JCS algorithm.

exchange.json contains synthetic requests and expected responses for publication, retries across packaging formats, updates, historical retries, another publisher's document, unauthorized updates, revision conflicts, and unsupported formats. Each request specifies its method, URL, headers, and a file containing the raw request body. Test credential-to-publisher mappings are recorded outside the requests. All credentials are public test placeholders.

The original HTML request uses content/dist/event.pai.html; event-updated.pai.html supplies the updated HTML request. unsupported.txt supplies an unsupported-format request. The exchange checks validate field shapes, status codes, and relationships between operations. The service tests exercise the corresponding HTTP behavior.

From the project root, run:

sh
npm run check:spec

Changes to fixtures need an explanation of the changed rule. Previously published files and acceptance records remain available for compatibility checks.
